neighbours.label: the verb 'pick' (pick / picked / picking), mostly in 'pick up'
fire: I never really picked up a guitar until I turned thirty.
After the storm we had to pick up the branches from the yard.
She stopped at the station to pick up her brother after work.
The team slowly picked up momentum in the second half.
He kept picking up bad habits from his older cousins.
Over the summer the shop picked up several new customers.
You can always pick yourself up and try again tomorrow.
The wind started picking up just as we left the harbor.
quiet: I never really played a guitar until I turned thirty.
After the storm we had to clear the branches from the yard.
She stopped at the station to meet her brother after work.
The team slowly gained momentum in the second half.
He kept learning bad habits from his older cousins.
Over the summer the shop attracted several new customers.
You can always dust yourself off and try again tomorrow.
The wind started blowing harder just as we left the harbor.
